# Row-level error diagnosis (executor X)

**Provenance.** Run `dev100_qwen35_4b_img_only_native_4c17aa3` (Qwen3.5-4B image-only, keyed JSON), generated by `uv run python scripts/row_error_diagnosis.py` (repo state `139186f+dirty`; ORACLE bootstrap 2000 doc-level paired resamples, seed 42). Every number is computed from the run's `predictions.json` / `trace.jsonl`, the gold labels, the OCR cache and the unmodified official scorer (`assignment/score.py` via `shipdoc.eval`). **All numbers UNVERIFIED** until a verifier recomputes them. Aggregates and counts only: no gold or predicted values, no names; value-level examples are in the local, outside-repo `<SHIPDOC_RUNS_DIR>/diagnosis/row_errors_local.md`.

## X1. row_missing / row_extra

### X1.0 Recount

`eval.error_taxonomy` (the respike definition) gives row_missing 89, row_extra 89, row_split_merge 0. ### X1.1 Breakdown (unpaired rows / all rows of the bucket)

`page position`: `only` = single-page doc, `first` / `middle` / `last` = page of a multipage doc (`middle` = a continuation page that is not the last). A gold row's page is the locator's row-to-page assignment (`locate.assign_rows` + `trainset.resolve_row_pages`, read-only); a predicted row's page is the trace page it was parsed from (replay of `merge_pages`' row loop). `near boundary` = first / last 3 rows of the page (gold order for gold rows, predicted order for predicted rows). ## X2. cpn / po null-status mismatches of paired rows

Scorer-paired invoice rows (full + partial pairs) with a customer_part_number / purchase_order null-status mismatch: 55. By kind: cpn_over_null 4, mixed 1, po_in_cpn_slot 50. Kinds: `po_in_cpn_slot` = gold cpn empty, predicted cpn equals the gold PO, predicted PO empty; `cpn_false_fill` / `po_false_fill` = gold empty, prediction filled; `cpn_over_null` / `po_over_null` = gold filled, prediction empty; `mixed` = both fields differ in null status in another way.

Per supplier group (every group with a mismatch, plus every group whose layout has a PO column but no customer-part column; layout columns from the gold of train+dev pooled: `not printed` = every gold row of the group has that column empty, a group-wide layout constant per recon; the last two columns = dev docs of the group whose OCR table-header line names a customer-part / a PO column, over dev docs with a detected header line):

| group | paired rows | mismatch rows | po_in_cpn_slot | other mismatches | cpn column (gold) | po column (gold) | OCR header names cpn col | OCR header names po col |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| inv_g03 | 29 | 3 | 0 | 3 | printed | not printed | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| inv_g05 | 17 | 0 | 0 | 0 | not printed | printed | 0/2 | 2/2 |
| inv_g06 | 38 | 0 | 0 | 0 | not printed | printed | 0/4 | 4/4 |
| inv_g09 | 96 | 1 | 0 | 1 | printed | printed | 7/7 | 7/7 |
| inv_g12 | 54 | 2 | 2 | 0 | not printed | printed | 0/8 | 8/8 |
| inv_g17 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 | not printed | printed | 0/2 | 2/2 |
| inv_g18 | 50 | 49 | 48 | 1 | not printed | printed | 0/3 | 3/3 |

The mismatches that are not `po_in_cpn_slot`, by group and kind: inv_g03 cpn_over_null 3, inv_g09 cpn_over_null 1, inv_g18 mixed 1.

`po_in_cpn_slot` rows: 50 (0 scanned, 50 digital) in 2 groups (inv_g12, inv_g18); groups whose gold layout prints NO customer-part column: 2 of 2; groups whose layout prints a PO column: 2 of 2; rows in a group without a customer-part column: 50 of 50. In these groups there is no customer-part column to read, so the model fills a column that does not exist: it writes the PO value into the cpn slot and leaves the PO slot empty.

Groups with the SAME layout class (PO column, no customer-part column) in dev and no `po_in_cpn_slot` row: inv_g05, inv_g06, inv_g17 (inv_g05: 17 paired rows, inv_g06: 38 paired rows, inv_g17: 7 paired rows). So the missing customer-part column is necessary-looking but NOT sufficient: the error is concentrated in the groups listed above.

Mixed groups (column printed on some rows only): 0.

Format shapes (digits -> 9, letters -> A) in the TRAIN gold: 2 cpn shapes, 2 PO shapes, 0 shared; 2 cpn-only and 2 PO-only shapes (basis of candidate rule R3).

## X4. Cause -> fix class -> ORACLE recoverable points

ORACLE replay (**ORACLE upper bound, not achievable**): the rows / cells of the cause are replaced by gold (pairs: the predicted row becomes the gold row; gold-only rows are appended; predicted-only rows are removed; slot mismatches get the gold cpn / po; waybill over-nulls get the gold value), then the unmodified scorer rescores the 100 dev docs. Delta = OVERALL points vs the run's 83.72; CI = paired doc-level bootstrap (2000 resamples, seed 42). Effects are NOT additive (OVERALL is a mean of per-doc scores and row F1 is a ratio); the combined rows are computed, not summed. Causes with zero rows are listed in X1.3 and have no ORACLE row.

| cause | n rows / cells | scanned / digital | fix class | recoverable OVERALL points [95% CI] (ORACLE upper bound, not achievable) | confidence in the classification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rows: column_shift | 65 gold / 65 pred (6 docs) | 31 / 34 | multi-page context strategy (column order of page 1 given to continuation pages) + fine-tune target (continuation-page rows) | +4.01 [+1.12, +7.20] | medium: most shifts sit on header-less continuation pages and the contrast holds inside supplier groups, but 7 docs, 13 shifts sit on pages with a header row, and the mechanism (missing column header) is inferred from OCR layout, not seen |
| rows: spn_misread | 24 gold / 24 pred (12 docs) | 16 / 8 | fine-tune target (glyph-level part-number reading); a plain nearest-OCR-span merge rule does not pay (R4) | +2.44 [+1.15, +3.89] | high: edit distance <= 2 or similarity >= 0.8 by the taxonomy rule; other fields right in most pairs; 28 docs |
| paired-row slot: cpn_over_null | 4 paired rows | 3 / 1 | not fixable at this n (a few cells) | +0.37 [+0.00, +1.00] | low |
| paired-row slot: mixed | 1 paired rows | 0 / 1 | not fixable at this n (a few cells) | +0.04 [+0.00, +0.15] | low |
| paired-row slot: po_in_cpn_slot | 50 paired rows | 0 / 50 | prompt / fine-tune target (a layout may have no customer-part column; the PO column is not the customer part); merge rule R3 (format-shape swap) also fixes it but rests on shapes of synthetic formats | +2.76 [+0.29, +5.91] | high: all rows are in groups whose gold layout has no customer-part column and a PO column |
| waybill header: mawb over-null | 9 cells | 7 / 2 | merge rule R2 (OCR pattern backfill) or fine-tune target (waybill-only schema) | +1.04 [+0.30, +1.99] | high: value and label are in the OCR text, the model emitted null |
| waybill header: carrier over-null | 3 cells | 1 / 2 | merge rule R1 (carrier from the model's own supplier_name slot) or prompt (carrier = letterhead company) | +0.35 [+0.00, +0.94] | high: the value sits in the supplier_name slot in all cases |
| waybill header: hawb over-null | 5 cells | 5 / 0 | merge rule R2 (OCR pattern backfill) or fine-tune target (waybill-only schema) | +0.24 [+0.05, +0.48] | medium: 2 cells |

Combined and group ORACLEs (computed jointly, so not the sum of the rows above):

| variant (ORACLE upper bound, not achievable) | OVERALL % | d OVERALL pts [95% CI] | d header acc pts | d row F1 pts | d fully correct pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| slot:all_null_status_mismatch | 87.10 | +3.38 [+0.72, +6.98] | +0.00 | +5.95 | +5.00 |
| header:all_waybill_over_nulls | 86.54 | +2.83 [+1.19, +4.56] | +2.07 | +0.00 | +10.00 |
| rows:all_unpaired_causes | 90.17 | +6.45 [+3.41, +9.66] | +0.00 | +9.63 | +13.00 |
| rows:unpaired + slot mismatches | 93.75 | +10.03 [+6.13, +14.34] | +0.00 | +15.58 | +19.00 |

Sum of the 8 single-cause deltas above = +11.26 pts vs the combined ORACLE +12.86 pts: the gap (+1.60) is the non-additivity (a doc's OVERALL has a fully-correct component, so fixing the last wrong cell of a doc is worth more than its cell share).

### Candidate merge-rule replays (achieved on dev, unmodified scorer, NOT oracles)

Four rules that follow from the findings above, replayed one at a time on the run's predictions. They are NOT upper bounds: they use only the model output, the OCR text and (R3) format shapes learned from TRAIN gold. R1 and R2 were designed after looking at the dev over-nulls, so their dev numbers are optimistic; R2's precision is also checked on all train+dev waybills in X3. `touched` = cells / rows the rule changed; `fixed` = wrong before, right after; `broken` = right before, wrong after.

| rule | touched | fixed | broken | wrong after | d OVERALL pts [95% CI] | d row F1 pts | d header acc pts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 waybill carrier <- own supplier_name slot | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | +0.35 [+0.00, +0.94] | +0.00 | +0.36 |
| R2 waybill mawb / hawb <- unique OCR pattern match | 14 | 14 | 0 | 0 | +2.08 [+0.80, +3.51] | +0.00 | +1.70 |
| R3 cpn <-> po slot swap by format shape (shapes from train gold) | 50 | 50 | 0 | 0 | +2.76 [+0.29, +5.91] | +5.41 | +0.00 |
| R4 part number <- nearest OCR span when absent from OCR | 60 | 13 | 38 | 47 | -2.60 [-4.25, -1.06] | -2.49 | +0.00 |

Mechanisms (one line per cause):

- `spn_misread`: the part number is the right line read with 1-2 wrong characters (see the edit profile in X1.3); the model, not the OCR layout, is the weak reader here and the OCR text is wrong too in a part of the cases, so snapping to it breaks as many rows as it fixes.
- `column_shift`: cpn / po / part-number values land one slot to the left or right; concentrated on continuation pages that carry no column-header row, where the model has to guess the column order.
- `spn_copies_other_slot`: the part-number slot is filled with the PO value of the same row (one doc, 17 rows), although the gold part number is readable in the OCR text.
- `page_short`: a page yields fewer rows than the gold page holds (one doc).
- `slot:po_in_cpn_slot`: layouts without a customer-part column: the PO value is written into the customer_part_number slot and purchase_order is left empty.
- `header:mawb`: the model emits a null mawb although MAWB value and label are on the page and in the OCR text; mostly scanned pages.
- `header:carrier`: the carrier is the letterhead company name (no 'carrier' label on any waybill); the model writes it into the invoice-schema supplier_name slot, which the merge drops.
- `header:hawb`: the model emits a null hawb although value and label are in the OCR text (scanned pages).
